recipes.name: Awesome Broccoli-Cheese Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk condensed soup, mayonnaise, egg, and onion together in a medium mixing bowl until combined.

Place frozen broccoli florets into a very large mixing bowl and break it up if necessary; add soup mixture and mix well to coat. Sprinkle with cheese and mix well; spread mixture into the prepared baking dish. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese has melted and the casserole is golden brown on top, 45 minutes to 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: I have been making this recipe for years but I do it a little differently - and ALWAYS get requests... 2 eggs beaten, 1 cup melted margarine, 1 cup HELLMAN's (not miracle whip) mayonnaise, 1 can cream of mushroom soup, 1 1/2 cups grated sharp cheddar cheese, 2 Tbsp chopped onion, 2 pkgs. frozen chopped broccoli, 1 small bag pepperidge farm stuffing mix. Cook & drain broccoli, mix everything else together (except stuffing mix), pour into greased casserole and top w/stuffing mix. Bake 350 for one hour. It is very important that you use real, full-fat ingredients such as mayonnaise and margarine. Otherwise it doesn't come out right. Also best when cools for at least 30 minutes before serving.

This was fabulous, but I did tweak it a bit to our liking. I used 1/2 c. sour cream and 1/2 c. mayo. Also added 12 ounces of sharp cheddar cheese, instead of only 8. Also did a crushed Ritz cracker with melter butter on top which is a definite in our family as we love that kind of topping. Made the night before Thanksgiving and it worked out great. I did not add the butter crumb topping until right before I was cooking it.

Broccoli casserole is far better using fresh broccoli, not frozen. I cook the broccoli until only partially cooked then add to remaining ingredients. Cover with foil before baking. Top with more shredded cheese and crushed crackers about 45 minutes in the oven and bake, uncovered another 10-15 minutes until cheese is melted and cracker crumbs are golden brown.

I loved it. However, if someone starts saying all the changes they made to your recipe that cook should start a post with that recipe. I’m not referring to anyone with a food restriction since that substitute might help another reader nor am I referring to simple statements such as, I changed type of soup. But if it’s basically another recipe or different category recipe then it’s not this recipe.

I made this on a -40° winter evening and my wife absolutely loved it saying "it tastes like a warm delicious hug". Only having one head of broccoli, I made a few tweaks to turn into a full one dish meal. Modifications: - 30oz of mixed vegetables (head of broccoli[crowned], one bell pepper[pieces], one large carrot[sliced], 6 small mushrooms[into sixths]) - Half cup mayo, half cup sour cream (thanks everyone) - Sautéed the onions with ~5 cloves of garlic and 4 diced boneless chicken thighs I know I diverged a bit from the recipe, but I think this recipe is great as a base and will 100% be making using it again.
A quick calculation means this recipe is over 3000 calories, so I substituted 6oz plain yogurt for the 8 oz mayonnaise, saving 1400 calories, and added 1/4 tsp cayenne to give it a little more zing.

I made it mostly as written, but made three changes: 1) used fresh broccoli instead of frozen; 2) subbed in 1/2 cup sour cream for 1/2 cup of the mayo; 3) doubled the amount of onions used, added some shallots as well, and fresh minced garlic, all of which I browned in butter before adding to the mixture. Overall it turned out very well, and was a hit at the Thanksgiving dinner where I served it. I would note that I was fairly generous with the "salt and pepper to taste," and I wonder if those who complain that the recipe is "bland" just didn't season it enough. When I make it again, I'm going to try some other variations, including: using cream of broccoli soup instead of mushroom; adding some additional herbs to the mixture, like thyme or oregano; adding a few splashes of sherry to the liquid.

I made as directed, doubling the recipe, for Friendsgiving last night and it disappeared quickly. I used Cabot Vermont Sharp cheese. Since it doesn't contain the yellow coloring some others do, the sauce looked a bit more elevated, almost like a Bechamel. If I make it again, I'd let the broccoli thaw and pat it dry.

This is a great casserole! For those who won’t use canned soup due to the high sodium content—there are now no-sodium cream soups that work great in casseroles OR you can make you own butter/flour/milk substitution, especially if you sauté your onions or fresh broccoli for the casserole. It’s delicious however you construct it. Do consider adding the cracker crumb topping, and it’s also great with some diced ham added to make it a complete meal. There are lots of variations. Even some crumbled bacon would be a nice touch. Making it your own way makes it more special.

I added some rotisserie chicken, some sliced mushrooms & a sprinkle of seasoning salt. Used 1/2 mayo + 1/2 sour cream. I also topped off the grated cheese with some home made bread stuffing. baked it for 45mins covered & then removed cover & browned it for 10mins more. Delicious.
Family loved this, but next day for leftovers, it was watery. When I made it again, I let frozen thaw and squeezed out water. Much better!
Simple, absolutely delicious ... this is definitely going in my rotation of vegetable dishes. Note - prior to baking, I placed fresh roma tomato slices in 2 rows (slightly overlapped) on top.
Made as is AWESOME SIDE DISH
Fantastic for sure
It is so easy to prepare. The taste is so good.

I usually add rice to my broccoli casserole but i have been trying to eat fewer carbs so this looked like a good option. Followed the recipe but used 2 bags of petite florets and 1/2 of the cheese. Added red pepper flakes. Tastes good. Cooked up nicely with crispy edges. Satisfying without being heavy. Will try again and add cauliflower and maybe a sharp cheddar.
Very good and easy
It was easy to make, turned out wonderful. I didnt change the recipe as this was the first time I made it. I may change something down the road but its not necessary for my family!

This recipe exceeded my expectations. It was easy to assemble, the flavors were a wonderful melding of cheese, mayonnaise and mushroom soup. It had the taste of a Sunday dinner. It is a classic casserole which could easily became a family tradition. I wish I had taken a photo.

My friend made this for me tonight as a belated birthday dinner. It was so delish I had to ask for the recipe! I'm a vegetarian, and I can think of so many ways to tweak this. Gets me excited to clean the birthday camping trip mess so I can cook. 😃
